neighbours.label: Start of the result clause in the 'so ADJ/much (that) …' construction: the subject pronoun or verb right after 'so … that' / 'so …,' and the 'to' of 'so … as to'; 'so' without a result clause and 'that' without 'so' are quiet
fire: The soup was so salty that it was sent back to the kitchen.
My cousins liked the cabin so much, they booked it again for August.
The lecture hall was so crowded that we had to stand at the back.
The instructions were so badly printed as to be almost useless.
The puppies were so tired that they fell asleep on the stairs.
The bridge had become so weak that it could not carry a truck.
The streets were so quiet that you could hear the river.
Her voice was so soft that they leaned forward to listen.
quiet: The soup was salty and it was sent back to the kitchen.
My cousins liked the cabin, and they booked it again for August.
The lecture hall was crowded, so we stood at the back.
The instructions were badly printed and almost useless.
I believe that they fell asleep on the stairs.
The engineer said that it could not carry a truck.
The streets were so quiet last night.
Her voice was very soft, and they leaned forward to listen.

notes: Card: 'so much, ⟦they⟧', 'so many ... that ⟦it⟧', 'so clearly expressed as ⟦to⟧', 'so exhausted ... that they ⟦were⟧'; the + pole is the ' and' inside 'so X and ...'. Probes: 0.64, 0.41, 0.47, 0.40, 0.28 for result clauses; 'icy and it was' 0.01, 'I think that it' 0.00, 'He was so happy.' 0.02.
